    Unbalanced Fixed-Effect PERMANOVA

    unbalanced-fixed-effects.Rmd

    Unequal cell sizes make the hypothesis definition part of the analysis. Phase 10 therefore requires an explicit Type I, II, or III request and exposes the estimable projector before calculating a p-value.

    Additive Type II inference with vegan::dune

    The management and moisture factors are unbalanced. In an additive model, Type II tests each factor after the other and is invariant to formula order.

    data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan")
bray <- vegan::vegdist(dune, method = "bray")
with(dune.env, table(Management, Moisture))
#>           Moisture
#> Management 1 2 4 5
#>         BF 2 1 0 0
#>         HF 3 0 1 1
#>         NM 1 1 0 4
#>         SF 1 2 1 2

design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Management + Moisture,
  dune.env,
  bray
)
hypotheses <- derive_unbalanced_hypotheses(
  design,
  hypothesis = "II"
)
lapply(hypotheses, function(x) {
  x[c("df", "nominal_df", "fully_estimable", "adjusted_for")]
})
#> $Management
#> $Management$df
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $Management$nominal_df
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $Management$fully_estimable
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $Management$adjusted_for
#> [1] "Moisture"
#> 
#> 
#> $Moisture
#> $Moisture$df
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $Moisture$nominal_df
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $Moisture$fully_estimable
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $Moisture$adjusted_for
#> [1] "Management"

fit <- permanova_unbalanced(
  design,
  hypothesis = "II",
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 20260718
)
fit$table
#>         term hypothesis df nominal_df       ss        ms denominator_df
#> 1 Management         II  3          3 0.892049 0.2973497             13
#> 2   Moisture         II  3          3 1.151622 0.3838741             13
#> 3   Residual       <NA> 13         13 1.678808 0.1291391             NA
#>   pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1 2.302554  0.007
#> 2 2.972564  0.003
#> 3       NA     NA

    Each term has its own reduced model and Freedman–Lane residual permutation, but both use the final full-model residual denominator.

    Type I follows formula order

    Sequential tests answer a different question. Reversing the formula can change the allocation of shared variation in an unbalanced design.

    forward <- permanova_unbalanced(
  design,
  hypothesis = "I",
  permutations = 0
)
reverse_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ Moisture + Management,
  dune.env,
  bray
)
reverse <- permanova_unbalanced(
  reverse_design,
  hypothesis = "I",
  permutations = 0
)
forward$table
#>         term hypothesis df nominal_df       ss        ms denominator_df
#> 1 Management          I  3          3 1.468592 0.4895306             13
#> 2   Moisture          I  3          3 1.151622 0.3838741             13
#> 3   Residual       <NA> 13         13 1.678808 0.1291391             NA
#>   pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1 3.790725     NA
#> 2 2.972564     NA
#> 3       NA     NA
reverse$table
#>         term hypothesis df nominal_df       ss        ms denominator_df
#> 1   Moisture          I  3          3 1.728165 0.5760550             13
#> 2 Management          I  3          3 0.892049 0.2973497             13
#> 3   Residual       <NA> 13         13 1.678808 0.1291391             NA
#>   pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1 4.460734     NA
#> 2 2.302554     NA
#> 3       NA     NA

    Type III needs an explicit parameterization

    For interactions, Type III retains every other term. Sum-to-zero contrasts are required so the factor hypotheses are explicit and reproducible.

    cells <- expand.grid(
  habitat = factor(c("reef", "sand")),
  season = factor(c("dry", "wet"))
)
counts <- c(3, 5, 4, 7)
sampling <- cells[rep(seq_len(nrow(cells)), counts), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(sampling) <- NULL
contrasts(sampling$habitat) <- contr.sum(2)
contrasts(sampling$season) <- contr.sum(2)

set.seed(20260718)
species <- 10
linear <- 1.3 +
  outer(sampling$habitat == "reef", seq(0.05, 0.25, length.out = species)) +
  outer(sampling$season == "wet", seq(-0.08, 0.18, length.out = species)) +
  outer(
    sampling$habitat == "reef" & sampling$season == "wet",
    seq(-0.05, 0.15, length.out = species)
  )
community <- matrix(
  rpois(length(linear), lambda = exp(linear)),
  nrow(sampling), species
)
factorial_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ habitat * season,
  sampling,
  vegan::vegdist(community, method = "bray")
)
type_three <- permanova_unbalanced(
  factorial_design,
  hypothesis = "III",
  permutations = 999,
  seed = 20260718
)
type_three$table
#>             term hypothesis df nominal_df         ss         ms denominator_df
#> 1        habitat        III  1          1 0.04488324 0.04488324             15
#> 2         season        III  1          1 0.03635983 0.03635983             15
#> 3 habitat:season        III  1          1 0.04107869 0.04107869             15
#> 4       Residual       <NA> 15         15 0.61572895 0.04104860             NA
#>    pseudo_f p_perm
#> 1 1.0934171  0.382
#> 2 0.8857751  0.574
#> 3 1.0007330  0.461
#> 4        NA     NA

    Incomplete cells and aliases

    Incomplete additive models may retain fully estimable main effects. An interaction model with aliased columns does not define the full Type III hypothesis and is rejected explicitly.

    selected <- !(sampling$habitat == "sand" & sampling$season == "wet")
incomplete <- droplevels(sampling[selected, , drop = FALSE])
contrasts(incomplete$habitat) <- contr.sum(2)
contrasts(incomplete$season) <- contr.sum(2)
incomplete_community <- community[selected, , drop = FALSE]
incomplete_design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ habitat * season,
  incomplete,
  vegan::vegdist(incomplete_community, method = "bray")
)
conditionMessage(tryCatch(
  permanova_unbalanced(
    incomplete_design,
    hypothesis = "III",
    permutations = 0
  ),
  error = identity
))
#> [1] "Type III inference requires a full-rank fixed model; aliased columns from incomplete cells are unsupported."

    Phase 10 supports fixed effects only. It does not manufacture an EMS denominator for unbalanced random, nested, crossed, or hybrid models. Those structures, partially estimable terms, and Type II main effects contained in interactions fail before inference.
